title: feat(plugin-view): ObjectView honours a spec-shaped named list view (objectui#8254)
body:
Fixes #8254

The renderer half objectui#7928's option A requires before `ObjectViewSchema.listViews` is mirrored by reference onto the protocol's `ObjectListViewSchema` — decision batch #70, 2026-09-07. The mirror is never shipped as a type-only edit, so the renderer honours the protocol's shape here and the declaration follows on that card.

## What the measurement found

The protocol declares a named view's `columns` as the union `string[] | ListColumn[]`. The local `NamedListView` declares only `string[]`. Two of the three routes out of `ObjectView` end in a **name slot** whose consumers index each record by every entry — `ObjectGridSchema.fields`, and the `fields` of the node `generateViewSchema` emits — and the named-view segment reached both of them **raw**.

Measured on the base tree by rendering a fixture built with `ObjectListViewSchema.parse(...)`: a named view carrying the `ListColumn[]` half arrived at both name slots as the column objects themselves, i.e. a non-empty field list naming nothing. That is verbatim the failure the header of `tableColumnFieldNames` already describes for `table.columns` — `ObjectKanban` skips its `highlightFields` fallback whenever the list is non-empty, so it renders worse than an empty one — and objectui#5269 already answered it at that boundary.

`viewColumnFieldNames` answers it at this one: the presence-preserving twin of that fold, over `columnIdentity`, this repo's single converged reader for "which field does this column entry name". It accepts no spelling `columnIdentity` did not already accept, so it narrows a declared union rather than widening a tolerated set. The **union** slots on the same branches — `ObjectGridSchema.columns` and the delegated `list-view` `columns` — keep taking the authored value raw, because their declared shape holds it and narrowing there would drop a column's own `label`. One value, two slots, each given the shape it declares.

Precedence does not move. An authored empty `columns` still stops the `||` chain where it stopped before — deliberately unlike the `table.columns` fold, whose fall-through to the deprecated `table.fields` alias is a precedence decision belonging to that chain alone. The only visible behaviour change is that column entries resolving to no identity now collapse to an empty list instead of reaching a name slot as nameless entries.

`filter` (spec rule objects, not the local tuple dialect), `sort`, `label` and `data` needed **no** renderer change. They are pinned anyway: "already works" is the claim that rots without an instrument.

Also gone: the stale `as any` on the named-view config's `label` read. It was not load-bearing — `label` is a declared member — and under the mirror `label` becomes optional, which the cast was hiding from the type checker at the one read site that has to survive its absence. Declared here rather than folded in silently.

## The pin

`packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/ObjectView.specShapedNamedView-8254.test.tsx` — 13 cases.

The spec leg of every fixture is built by running `ObjectListViewSchema.parse(...)`, not by looking spec-shaped. A fixture that merely resembles the protocol pins the author's memory of it; one that has been through the protocol's own parser cannot drift from it, and the schema is strict upstream, so the parse also proves the fixture carries no local-dialect key.

Both legs ride **one** fixture, side by side in the same `expect`, which is what the card asked for: asserting each leg against a hard-coded literal in two separate cases would let both drift together and still pass.

## Reverse verification — and where the prediction was wrong

Reverting the two `viewColumnFieldNames(...)` call sites to their raw forwards, on the committed fix:

```
anchor occurrences BEFORE mutation: 2  (expect 2)
python replaced 2 occurrence(s)
anchor occurrences AFTER mutation: 0 (expect 0); raw-forward occurrences: 2 (expect 2)
HEAD blob:    db4c76a1e36047def04648501fcac83f9b23a99e
mutated blob: e90ba0ad823b3fb2d5590b3c1be0d71601d1525e
  Test Files  1 failed (1)
       Tests  3 failed | 10 passed (13)
RESTORED: byte-identical to HEAD (db4c76a1e36047def04648501fcac83f9b23a99e)
```

Predicted: the four `columns` cases red. **Measured: three, and the prediction was wrong about which three.** Two of those four assert a union slot the fix never touched, so they stayed green exactly as they should — they are controls, not fix cases, and the prediction had mis-sorted them; the third red came from the controls block instead, the no-identity case, which rides the fold. The miss is recorded in the test file's own header rather than re-fitted to the result.

The mutation reached the code under test directly: the test imports `../ObjectView` by relative path, so no `dist/` sits between the edit and the run. Both legs proved the edit on disk by occurrence count and by `git hash-object` against the `HEAD` blob, and the restore is proved by the blob hash plus an empty `git diff HEAD`, never by an exit code.

| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-view type-check` | 0 |

| `check-control-bytes` · `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` | 0 · 0 |

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` lives in the sibling `objectstack` checkout and **refuses** for objectui paths (exit 2, "a sister repo's list is hand-derived from its own package manifest and its own workflow files"), so this list was hand-derived from this repo's own `package.json` scripts and `.github/workflows/`.

**Declared narrowing.** The manifest carries ninety-odd `check:*` scripts. This run is the subset whose **input** this diff can move, plus the two pins that re-derive from the edited file by AST — `object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.test.ts` and app-shell's `ObjectView.relayRungCensus-7559.test.ts`, both of which parse `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`. The rest is the whole farm and belongs to CI. `check-changeset-claims` reported five pending changesets naming the edited file; all five were read and none is falsified by this diff — they describe the non-grid fetch, the gantt branch of `generateViewSchema`, the `title` composition and the `viewTabBar` census, none of which this change touches.

Type-check needed the dependency closure built first (`turbo run build --filter '@object-ui/plugin-view^...'`, exit 0); without it `tsc` reports missing workspace `.d.ts` files, which is not a finding about this diff.

## Acceptance notes

**The card's `data` sub-decision is already answered, and its stated premise is dead.** The card describes an undeclared `data` reached through a cast on the named-view config. On today's tree: `data` **is** declared on `NamedListView` — by reference to the spec type, not a hand copy — the cast is **gone**, and the protocol's own `ObjectListViewSchema` declares `data` too. objectui#8980 landed all of it under the director-seat ruling of 2026-09-13. The default direction on this card ("remove the read") would now delete a read of a member both faces declare, which the file's own comment forbids by name, so the read stands unchanged and this PR decides nothing about it. Authored population carrying an inline `data` block on a named view: **zero**, measured structurally over every authored named view in `apps/`, `examples/` and `content/`, with a live grep channel as the control.

**The card's member figures are stale.** "47 declared members, 6 read" was the pre-objectui#8980 reading. The instrument that re-derives both numbers is `object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.test.ts`; read the counts there rather than from this paragraph. Of the members the renderer reads off a named view, exactly one has no counterpart in `ObjectListViewSchema`: `options`, the untyped bag. Every other one maps.

**The card's line anchor does not point where it says.** Re-derived anchors are reported on the card.

**The landing package is `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`**, re-derived: `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` contains zero occurrences of the named-view binding this card is about.

**Population count, for the conversion note the mirror will need.** Twelve authored named views across `apps/` + `examples/` + `content/`; `apps/` contributes none. Five are accepted by `ObjectListViewSchema` as written, seven are refused — six for the now-required `columns`, two for the tuple filter dialect. The refusals concentrate in the documentation examples, so objectui#7928's mirror needs a docs pass shipped with it. Counts taken on this card, on this tree; re-run the census before acting on them.

**Not filed, noted only:** the `views`-prop segment beside the named-view one at both name slots still forwards raw. It declares `string[]` and is the objectui#5097 host-composition surface, so its contract has not moved and there is nothing to honour yet; when a host writes column objects there, it is that surface's card. The named-view `sort` is a second, narrower asymmetry: `ObjectListViewSchema` still admits a bare string sort clause while objectui retired that spelling under decision batch #77 and refuses it in the grid path. Both are recorded for whoever lands the mirror, not carried here.

objectui#7928 is `pm:blocked` on this card and is **not** closed by this pull request; it remains open, and its own half — the by-reference declaration — is still to come.
